original_record.question: A parallelogram contains two identical regular hexagons. The hexagons share a common side, and each has two sides touching the sides of the parallelogram. What fraction of the parallelogram's area is shaded? <image1>
original_record.solution: The regular hexagons have interior angles of $120^{\circ}$ and fit into the corners of the parallelogram, so the parallelogram must have interior angles of $120^{\circ}$ and $60^{\circ}$.  ![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2023_12_27_0f4ed2787981bb911326g-090.jpg?height=180&width=337&top_left_y=433&top_left_x=1522)  Therefore the diagonals of the hexagons drawn are parallel to the edges of the parallelogram. By extending these diagonals, the parallelogram is dissected into eight trapezia. The four trapezia in the hexagons are clearly all congruent because their interior angles are $60^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}, 120^{\circ}, 120^{\circ}$ and their three shorter sides are all the same length (being equal to the length of the sides of the hexagons). The other four have the same interior angles as these and their three shorter sides are easily seen to have the same length as the sides of the hexagons. Hence the parallelogram has been dissected into eight congruent trapezia, so the shaded area is half the total area.
